content:
The test image shows a single mango leaf that is completely brown, desiccated, and curled — no green tissue remains. This indicates complete tissue death rather than a fungal coating (Sooty_Mould shows black patches on still-green leaves), spots (Anthracnose), or powdery coating (Powdery_Mildew).

The complete browning and withering of the leaf from tip to base is characteristic of **Die_Back**, where shoots and leaves die progressively due to fungal infection (typically *Lasiodiplodia theobromae*), resulting in fully dried, brown, shriveled leaves.
